input: Hi doctor,I am a 19 year old female weighing 100 lbs and 5.6 feet tall. I have had splinter hemorrhages that started in my index finger and now has spread to my thumb, but the pain in spreading to four fingers of my right hand. It becomes unbearable at times when I wake up or when I go into cold environments. I have no heart problems that I know of besides an abnormally high heart rate for the past two years, which has been dismissed by a doctor as nothing serious. I am concerned because of the pain it has caused me, and I am certain I have not had any trauma to my nails. It is spreading with time. I am not taking any regular medicine except Ortho Tri-Cyclen Lo (birth control).
answer_icliniq: Hello, Welcome to Chat Doctor forum. There is a possibility of limb ischemia that is obstruction of blood flow to your hand. As it is progressive, it is likely due to an embolus (clot) getting dislodged and landing in your hand or may be due to local clot formation. I suggest you visit your specialist doctor and get the following tests done. Oral birth control pill could have a role to play, as it makes blood thicker. Limb ischemia is an emergency, and it is crucial that we rule out this possibility as the consequences may not be good. So, visit ER (emergency room) and get yourself examined as soon as possible. Is there any discoloration like bluish tinge or erythematous coloration? Can you upload the photo of your hand? Revert with more information to an internal medicine physician online
answer_chatgpt: Hello, it sounds like you may be experiencing a condition called nail bed splinter hemorrhages. This can be caused by several underlying conditions, including vascular disease, infection, or trauma. Given that you have no known history of heart problems, I would suggest visiting your primary care doctor or a dermatologist for an evaluation. They may perform a thorough physical exam and blood tests to determine the underlying cause of your symptoms. Additionally, they may recommend treatment options such as medication, nail bed surgery or laser therapy depending on the underlying cause.

input: Hello doctor,I have PBC stage 4, Gave, COPD, Hashimoto\s, etc. I have been around someone who was just diagnosed with mono. I have used her water bottle. Should I be worried and, if so, what symptom could I develop? Do I have to stay away from this person now? I am currently under Urso 300 mg six per day.
answer_icliniq: Hello, Welcome to the ChatDoctor. I can understand your concern. Do not worry, and I will clear your doubt. Infectious mononucleosis usually caused by EBV (Epstein-Barr), and it can spread through saliva mainly. So sharing of the objects like water bottle or glass object can spread infection. So you are at risk of spending it. But do not be panic. The symptoms are fever and sore throat, mainly with enlarged cervical nodes. Splenomegaly also can occur. If fever, malaise, and sore throat occur than investigate by CBC (complete blood count) and serological test for EBV, which includes ESP (extrasensory perception), Ig M (immunoglobulin M), and Elisa (Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay). Infectious mononucleosis usually resolves by its own with time. Anyway if you suffer from fever and sore throat that will discuss further and you can consult a nearby physician for examination at that time. It is advisable not to share an object with an infected person. I hope this will help you. Get back with more query if you still have doubt.
answer_chatgpt:
As an AI language model, I don't have access to your medical history or current health status. However, I can provide some general information. 

Mono (infectious mononucleosis) is a viral illness caused by the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV). It is typically spread through saliva, so sharing drinks or utensils can increase the risk of transmission. 

If you have PBC stage 4, GAVE, COPD, Hashimoto's, and other medical conditions, it is crucial to take extra precautions to avoid getting sick. Mono can be challenging to diagnose in adults and may cause symptoms such as fever, sore throat, swollen lymph nodes, fatigue, and body aches. Some people may not have any symptoms at all.

It is recommended to avoid sharing utensils or personal items with someone who has been diagnosed with mono. If you have used someone else's water bottle, it is best to clean it thoroughly before using it again. If you develop any symptoms, such as a sore throat or fatigue, contact your doctor immediately. 

In addition, it's important to continue taking your medication as prescribed and follow any other medical advice provided by your doctor. Stay up to date with vaccinations and practice good hygiene, such as frequent hand washing, to reduce the risk of getting sick.
answer_chatdoctor: 1) Please do not worry. Mononucleosis is an infection caused by Epstein-Barr virus (EBV). It can cause fever, sore throat, swollen lymph nodes, fatigue, headache, body aches, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and muscle pain.2) The risk of developing serious complications after mononucleosis is low, but it is important to know that they can occur. Complications include meningitis, encephalitis, heart problems, hepatitis, and jaundice.3) You should avoid close contact with people who may be carrying the virus as it can spread through saliva or other secretions. You did not mention your age. If you are young enough, you are unlikely to suffer any complications. But, if you are over 55 years old you maybe at higher risk for serious complications.
